t: Section 583 of the Foreign Relations Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 1994 and 1995 (Public Law 103–236) is amended by striking  “July 1, 1995” and inserting in lieu thereof “August 15, 1995”.

fable.w: This section only changes a date in an existing statute, replacing July 1, 1995 with August 15, 1995. There is no tempting reading here: it creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment that changes a specific date in a previous statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely an internal legislative adjustment.
qwen_block.s: Section 583 of the Foreign Relations Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 1994 and 1995 (Public Law 103–236) is amended by striking “July 1, 1995” and inserting in lieu thereof “August 15, 1995”.

opus.w: This section only amends a prior statute by changing a deadline from "July 1, 1995" to "August 15, 1995." It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The underlying Section 583 might involve some process, but the text being labelled is a technical date change with no outside-party participation.
opus.b: Reading this as participation would mean importing whatever Section 583 of Public Law 103–236 requires. But this section only changes a date. On its own text, nothing here involves anyone outside the federal government in a decision.
